question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Slightly ______ bitter oranges to remove the red color which covers their skins.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. grate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a verb in the imperative form that means to rub food against a rough surface so as to shred it. "Grate" is exactly that verb — one grates the peel (skin) of oranges to take off the outer red/orange layer. (कद्दूकस करना)

◦ Correct: Slightly grate bitter oranges to remove the red color which covers their skins.

• The sentence is a recipe-style instruction, so a bare imperative verb ("grate") is required, not a noun or an adjective.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "great" is an adjective meaning very good/large — it cannot act as the verb of the sentence.

• Option 3 "grace" as a verb means to honour or adorn something; it does not mean to scrape off a skin.

• Option 4 "grade" means to arrange or rank in grades/classes — again it does not fit "to remove the red color".

NOTE

• Watch out for such homophone-like confusables in SSC papers: grate (to shred / a fireplace frame) vs great (excellent), grate on (to irritate). Related kitchen verbs: grate, peel, mince, chop, dice, whisk.

question: Select the wrongly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Pausity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pausity" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Paucity", which means scarcity; the presence of something in only very small quantities. (कमी / अल्पता)

◦ Example: There is a paucity of reliable data on rural employment.

• Spelling key: PAU + CI + TY (the sound is /s/ but the letter is c, as in "paucity", "scarcity", "capacity").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Phlegmatic" (correct) — having an unemotional, calm and stolidly composed temperament. (शांत स्वभाव वाला)

• "Philistine" (correct) — a person who is hostile or indifferent to culture and the arts. (कलाविमुख व्यक्ति)

• "Philanthropy" (correct) — the desire to promote the welfare of others, expressed especially by generous donation of money. (परोपकार)

NOTE

• Words from the Greek root phil- ("love"): philanthropy (love of mankind), philosophy (love of wisdom), bibliophile (lover of books), philology (love of words/language).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Wealthy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Affluent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Wealthy" means having a great deal of money, property or possessions; rich. Its closest synonym among the options is "affluent", which also means rich and prosperous. (धनी / समृद्ध)

◦ Example: They live in an affluent (wealthy) neighbourhood of the city.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Depressed" means sad/dejected (or, of an area, suffering economic hardship) — it is not a synonym of wealthy.

• Option 3 "Lacking" means deficient or missing something — the opposite idea.

• Option 4 "Poor" is the direct antonym of wealthy.

NOTE

• Synonyms of wealthy: affluent, prosperous, well-off, well-heeled, opulent, moneyed.

• Antonyms of wealthy: poor, needy, destitute, impoverished, penniless, indigent.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A calculated move to gain an advantage
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Gambit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "gambit" is a device, action or opening remark that is calculated to gain an advantage. The word comes from chess, where a gambit is an opening in which a player sacrifices a pawn to gain a positional advantage. (सोची-समझी चाल)

◦ Example: Offering a discount was a clever gambit to attract new customers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Grunt" — a low, short guttural sound made by an animal or a person. (घुरघुराना)

• Option 2 "Bonsai" — the Japanese art of growing ornamental, artificially dwarfed trees in pots.

• Option 4 "Profit" — financial gain; the difference between the amount earned and the amount spent. It is a result, not a calculated move.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes often asked in SSC: stratagem/ploy (a cunning plan), ruse (a trick to deceive), manoeuvre (a skilful movement or plan), gambit (an opening move made to gain an advantage).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

If the dog (is allow complete freedom), it can assume that any toy is acceptable for play.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. is allowed complete freedom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause needs the passive voice: "is + past participle (V3)". The past participle of "allow" is "allowed", so the correct structure is "is allowed complete freedom".

◦ Correct: If the dog is allowed complete freedom, it can assume that any toy is acceptable for play.

• The subject "the dog" is singular, so the auxiliary must be "is", not "are".

• "Complete" is an adjective and correctly modifies the noun "freedom".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "allowed completely freedom" — the adverb "completely" cannot modify the noun "freedom"; it also drops the auxiliary "is".

• Option 3 "No substitution required" is wrong because "is allow" is ungrammatical (auxiliary + base form is not a valid passive).

• Option 4 "are allowed complete free" — wrong number ("are" with the singular "dog") and "free" (adjective) is used where the noun "freedom" is needed.

NOTE

• Passive voice pattern: object + be (am/is/are/was/were) + V3 (+ by agent). Example: The rules are enforced strictly. Always check (i) subject–verb agreement and (ii) that the main verb is in the third form.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

Social media is ______ to market products.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. used.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the auxiliary "is", a past participle (V3) is required to form the passive voice. The V3 of "use" is "used".

◦ Correct: Social media is used to market products.

• The sense is passive: social media is not doing the using — it is the thing that is used (by people/companies) in order to market products.

• "to market products" is an infinitive of purpose ("in order to market products"), which fits neatly after the passive verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "uses" — "is uses" is ungrammatical (two finite verbs together).

• Option 3 "use" — "is use" is not a valid structure; the base form cannot follow "is".

• Option 4 "using" would make it active continuous ("is using"), which would wrongly suggest that social media itself is marketing products, and it also leaves the sentence without an object.

NOTE

• Structures after be: be + V3 = passive (is written); be + V4/-ing = continuous (is writing). Also learn the fixed pattern "be used to + noun/-ing" (be accustomed to) vs "used to + V1" (past habit).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

What customs officials are asking for are not things that _______ their own personal titles.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. aggrandize.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Aggrandize" means to increase the power, status, wealth or reputation of someone; to enhance or make greater. Things that "aggrandize their own personal titles" are things that add to their personal standing. (बढ़ाना / महिमामंडित करना)

◦ Correct: ... are not things that aggrandize their own personal titles.

• The blank needs a transitive verb that can take "their own personal titles" as its object — only "aggrandize" and "advocate" are transitive here, and only "aggrandize" gives the required sense of enlarging one's status.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "accede" means to agree to a demand or to take up an office; it is intransitive and takes "to" (accede to a request).

• Option 3 "acerbic" is an adjective (sharp and forthright in tone), so it cannot be the verb of the clause.

• Option 4 "advocate" means to publicly recommend or support; one does not "advocate a title".

NOTE

• Word family: aggrandize (verb), aggrandizement (noun — "self-aggrandizement" means the act of increasing one's own power or importance). Synonyms: magnify, exalt, enhance, elevate. Antonyms: belittle, diminish, demean.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Forciing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Forciing" is incorrectly spelt. The correct spelling is "Forcing" — the present participle of the verb "force" (to compel somebody to do something). (मजबूर करना)

◦ Spelling rule: when a verb ends in a silent -e, the -e is dropped before adding -ing: force → forcing, make → making, write → writing, come → coming.

• The extra "i" in "forciing" makes it wrong; there is never a double "i" in such forms.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Trust" (correct) — firm belief in the reliability or truth of someone/something. (विश्वास)

• "Shopping" (correct) — here the final consonant is doubled because "shop" is a short verb ending in a single vowel + single consonant: shop → shopping (also stop → stopping, run → running).

• "Wave" (correct) — a moving ridge of water; to move the hand to and fro.

NOTE

• Three key -ing rules: (i) drop silent -e (hope → hoping); (ii) double the final consonant after a short stressed vowel (begin → beginning); (iii) -ie changes to -y (die → dying, lie → lying).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

It's good to travel and / work, most beautiful than going / to the same office each day.
option_3: to the same office each day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. work, most beautiful than going.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" signals a comparison between two things, and a comparison always takes the comparative degree, never the superlative. Hence "most beautiful than" is wrong; it must be "more beautiful than".

◦ Correct: It's good to travel and work, more beautiful than going to the same office each day.

• "Beautiful" is a long adjective (3 syllables), so its comparative is formed with "more" and its superlative with "the most".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment "It's good to travel and" is correct — "It is good to + V1" is a standard structure.

• Segment "to the same office each day." is correct — "each day" is a proper adverbial of frequency.

• Because a definite error exists, "No error" cannot be the answer.

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: beautiful – more beautiful – most beautiful; good – better – best; bad – worse – worst. Rule: use the comparative with "than" and the superlative with "the" / "of all" / "in the class". Never write "more better" or "most beautiful than".

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

It would be neat and / cleanest, a home worthy of / spending our lives together.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. cleanest, a home worthy of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The two adjectives joined by "and" must be in the same degree (parallel structure). The first is "neat" — a positive degree adjective — so the second must also be positive: "clean", not the superlative "cleanest".

◦ Correct: It would be neat and clean, a home worthy of spending our lives together.

• A superlative such as "cleanest" also needs a group to compare within (e.g., "the cleanest house in the town"), which is absent here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment "It would be neat and" is correct — "would be" expresses a hypothetical/future-in-the-past idea.

• Segment "spending our lives together." is correct — "worthy of + V-ing" is the standard pattern (worthy of praise / worthy of spending).

• Since a clear error exists, "No error" is not the answer.

NOTE

• Parallelism is a favourite SSC topic: items joined by and/or/but must share the same grammatical form — "neat and clean", "reading and writing", "not only fast but also accurate".

question:
Select the word from the options which is similar in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

There is widespread (prejudice) against workers over 45.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Intolerance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Prejudice" means a preconceived opinion or unfair bias against a person or group that is not based on reason or actual experience. The closest option is "intolerance" — an unwillingness to accept views, beliefs or people different from one's own. (पूर्वाग्रह / असहिष्णुता)

◦ Correct sense: There is widespread intolerance (prejudice) against workers over 45.

• The phrase "prejudice against" clearly indicates hostility/bias, which "intolerance" captures.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Concern" means worry or interest — it is neutral and far weaker than prejudice.

• Option 3 "Temperament" means a person's nature or disposition.

• Option 4 "Misfortune" means bad luck.

NOTE

• Synonyms of prejudice: bias, partiality, bigotry, intolerance, preconception, discrimination.

• Antonyms of prejudice: impartiality, fairness, open-mindedness, tolerance. Note the related word prejudicial (harmful to someone's interests).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Can we reschedule the meeting? I ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. have a headache.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With ailments the standard collocation in English is "have + a/an + illness": have a headache, have a cold, have a fever, have a toothache. The speaker is describing a condition happening now, so the simple present "I have a headache" is right. (मुझे सिरदर्द है)

◦ Correct: Can we reschedule the meeting? I have a headache.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "take a headache" is not an English collocation — we take medicine, a rest or a break, not a headache.

• Option 3 "get a headache" means the headache starts/develops (a repeated or future event, e.g., "I get a headache whenever I read in the dark"); it does not state a present condition.

• Option 4 "give a headache" would mean causing someone else pain ("This noise gives me a headache").

NOTE

• Useful health collocations: have a cough/cold/fever/sore throat; catch a cold; suffer from asthma; come down with the flu; take medicine; feel dizzy.

question:
Select the word from the options which is exactly opposite in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

She relished our (arguments), most of which she won.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. agreements.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Arguments" here means heated disagreements or verbal disputes. Its exact antonym is "agreements" — situations of harmony and shared opinion. (तर्क-वितर्क / झगड़े का विलोम — सहमति)

◦ Contrast: They had frequent arguments, but finally reached several agreements.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "feud" — a long-running bitter quarrel: a synonym, not an antonym.

• Option 2 "negotiations" — discussions aimed at reaching a deal; a process, not the opposite of a quarrel.

• Option 4 "altercation" — a noisy quarrel: again a synonym of argument.

NOTE

• Synonyms of argument (quarrel sense): dispute, altercation, squabble, row, feud, wrangle.

• Antonyms: agreement, accord, concord, consensus, harmony. (Note that "argument" can also mean a reason put forward in support of an idea.)

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the bracketed idiom in the given sentence.

He is (a wolf in sheep's clothing), outwardly kind but inwardly vicious!
option_3: A situation involving a narrow escape from danger
option_4: Angry today about something that occurred in the past
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A dangerous person pretending harmless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a wolf in sheep's clothing" means a dangerous or harmful person who pretends to be gentle and harmless. The rest of the sentence — "outwardly kind but inwardly vicious" — explains the idiom exactly. (भेड़ की खाल में भेड़िया)

◦ Example: Beware of that broker; he is a wolf in sheep's clothing.

• The expression comes from Aesop's fable and also from a Biblical warning about false prophets.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 describes the idiom "to tear someone off a strip / haul over the coals" (to scold).

• Option 3 describes "a close shave / a narrow escape".

• Option 4 describes holding "a grudge" or "raking up the past".

NOTE

• Related idioms of deceit: "cry wolf" (raise a false alarm), "crocodile tears" (insincere sorrow), "snake in the grass" (a treacherous person), "two-faced" (hypocritical).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

We was installing wood flooring throughout our house.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. installed wood.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "We" is plural, so the singular auxiliary "was" is wrong; "was installing" cannot go with "we" (it would have to be "were installing"). The sentence simply reports a completed past action, so the simple past "installed" is the best correction.

◦ Correct: We installed wood flooring throughout our house.

• "Wood flooring" is a standard noun + noun compound (like "wood panelling", "stone flooring"), so "wood" need not become "wooden".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No improvement" is wrong because "We was" violates subject–verb agreement.

• Option 3 "installs wood" is the singular present form and does not agree with "We" (we install / he installs).

• Option 4 "installs wooden" repeats that agreement error and needlessly changes the compound noun.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement with "be": I was; he/she/it was; we/you/they were. In the present: I am, he/she/it is, we/you/they are. Use the simple past for a finished action with no continuing sense.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

I had been angry the whole / evening, so she rubs brahmi / oil into my scalp to cool my brain.
option_1: oil into my scalp to cool my brain.
option_4: I had been angry the whole
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. evening, so she rubs brahmi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first clause is in the past perfect continuous/past tense ("I had been angry the whole evening"), so the verb in the following clause must also be in the past. The present tense "rubs" breaks this sequence of tenses; it should be "rubbed".

◦ Correct: I had been angry the whole evening, so she rubbed brahmi oil into my scalp to cool my brain.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Segment "I had been angry the whole" is correct — "had been + adjective" with a duration ("the whole evening") is fine.

• Segment "oil into my scalp to cool my brain." is correct — "rub something into" is the right collocation and "to cool" is an infinitive of purpose.

• As a definite tense error exists, "No error" is not the answer.

NOTE

• Rule of sequence of tenses: if the principal clause is in a past tense, the subordinate clause is normally also in a past tense (He said that he was ill). Exception: universal truths stay in the present (He said that the sun rises in the east).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

In fits and starts
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Irregularly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "in fits and starts" means irregularly; with many stops and starts; not steadily or continuously. (रुक-रुक कर)

◦ Example: The old engine ran in fits and starts all the way home.

◦ Example: He studies in fits and starts, which is why his marks fluctuate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Be in difficulty" is the sense of idioms like "in hot water" or "in a fix".

• Option 3 "Everywhere" corresponds to "far and wide" or "high and low".

• Option 4 "Summary" corresponds to "in a nutshell" or "in brief".

NOTE

• Similar idioms of manner: "by fits and starts" (same meaning), "off and on / on and off" (occasionally), "now and then" (sometimes), "round the clock" (continuously — the opposite idea).

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Plain
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Fancy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As an adjective, "plain" means simple, undecorated, without any ornament or elaboration. Its antonym is "fancy", meaning elaborate, decorated or ornamental. (सादा का विलोम — सजावटी / भड़कीला)

◦ Contrast: She wore a plain cotton saree, not a fancy silk one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Stupid" (foolish) is unrelated — the opposite of "clever", not of "plain".

• Option 3 "Crazy" (mad) is not the opposite of plain.

• Option 4 "Mean" (unkind or stingy) is the opposite of "generous/kind".

NOTE

• "Plain" has several senses: simple/undecorated (opposite: fancy, ornate); clear and easy to understand (opposite: obscure); frank ("plain speaking"); and as a noun, a large flat stretch of land (e.g., the Northern Plains).

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Urging or requesting (someone) solemnly or earnestly to do something
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Adjure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Adjure" means to urge or request someone solemnly or earnestly to do something, often as though under oath. (सत्यनिष्ठा से आग्रह करना)

◦ Example: The judge adjured the witness to tell the whole truth.

• It is the only verb among the options; the other three are nouns, so they cannot express an action of urging.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Arrears" — money that is owed and should have been paid earlier. (बकाया)

• Option 3 "Armada" — a fleet of warships (famously the Spanish Armada of 1588).

• Option 4 "Arena" — a level area surrounded by seating, used for sports or entertainment.

NOTE

• Similar verbs: implore/beseech (to beg earnestly), exhort (to strongly encourage), entreat (to ask earnestly), enjoin (to instruct or urge to do something). Note also the word family: adjure (verb) → adjuration (noun).

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

How (can a book such as) be written before I'd lived the incidents it described?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. could such a book.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct word order is "such a + noun" (determiner + article + noun), so it must be "such a book", not "a book such as". "Such as" is used only when examples follow (e.g., "fruits such as mangoes").

◦ Correct: How could such a book be written before I'd lived the incidents it described?

• The rest of the sentence is in the past ("before I'd lived"), so the past modal "could" agrees with the tense far better than the present "can".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No correction required" is wrong because "a book such as be written" is ungrammatical.

• Option 3 "must so a book" is meaningless — "so" cannot replace "such" before a noun.

• Option 4 "may such a book" has the right word order but the wrong modal: "may" expresses permission/possibility in the present, clashing with the past-perfect "I'd lived".

NOTE

• such vs so: use "such + (a/an) + adjective + noun" (such a good film) and "so + adjective/adverb" (so good, so quickly). Modal pairs: can → could, will → would, may → might, shall → should.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

At the core of the (1) ______ lies the fierce (2) ______ between two branches of the Kuru dynasty, the Pandavas and the Kauravas. The lifelong struggle (3) ______ the cousins for the throne of Hastinapur culminates (4) ______ bloody battle of Kurukshetra, in which (5) ______ kings of that period participated and perished.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. epic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage describes the Mahabharata — the Kuru dynasty, the Pandavas and the Kauravas, and the battle of Kurukshetra. The Mahabharata is an "epic", i.e., a long narrative poem about heroic deeds. So "At the core of the epic lies the fierce rivalry ..." is the natural reading. (महाकाव्य)

◦ Correct: At the core of the epic lies the fierce rivalry between two branches of the Kuru dynasty ...

• The blank follows "the", so a noun is required, and "epic" is the only option that works as a noun here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "dull" and 3 "bright" are adjectives and give no sense after "the core of the ...".

• Option 2 "exercise" is a noun but is contextually absurd — an exercise has no "fierce rivalry between two branches of a dynasty" at its core.

NOTE

• "Epic" as an adjective means heroic or grand in scale ("an epic journey"). The two great Indian epics are the Ramayana and the Mahabharata; the Mahabharata, attributed to Ved Vyasa, is the longest epic poem in the world.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

At the core of the (1) ______ lies the fierce (2) ______ between two branches of the Kuru dynasty, the Pandavas and the Kauravas. The lifelong struggle (3) ______ the cousins for the throne of Hastinapur culminates (4) ______ bloody battle of Kurukshetra, in which (5) ______ kings of that period participated and perished.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. rivalry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank sits between the adjective "fierce" and the phrase "between two branches of the Kuru dynasty", so it needs a noun denoting competition or enmity. "Rivalry" means a state of intense competition or hostility between people or groups. (प्रतिद्वंद्विता)

◦ Correct: ... lies the fierce rivalry between two branches of the Kuru dynasty, the Pandavas and the Kauravas.

• "Fierce rivalry" is also a very common collocation in English.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "commute" means to travel regularly between home and work — completely out of context.

• Option 3 "hostile" is an adjective (unfriendly); the noun form "hostility" would have fitted, but the adjective cannot follow "the fierce".

• Option 4 "friendship" contradicts "fierce" and the whole idea of a lifelong struggle.

NOTE

• Synonyms of rivalry: competition, contention, opposition, antagonism, feud. Antonyms: cooperation, friendship, alliance, harmony.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

At the core of the (1) ______ lies the fierce (2) ______ between two branches of the Kuru dynasty, the Pandavas and the Kauravas. The lifelong struggle (3) ______ the cousins for the throne of Hastinapur culminates (4) ______ bloody battle of Kurukshetra, in which (5) ______ kings of that period participated and perished.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. between.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The struggle is between two identifiable sides — the Pandavas and the Kauravas, described as "the cousins" (the two branches of the Kuru dynasty). For two parties, English uses the preposition "between". (के बीच)

◦ Correct: The lifelong struggle between the cousins for the throne of Hastinapur ...

• Also, "struggle/conflict/war between X and Y" is the standard collocation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "amongst" (a variant of "among") is used for more than two, or for an undivided group — here only two rival branches are meant.

• Option 2 "inside" refers to position within an enclosure, not to a relationship.

• Option 4 "along" means beside/following the length of something.

NOTE

• Preposition rule: between = two persons/things clearly distinguished ("between you and me"); among/amongst = more than two, or a mass ("share it among the five of you"). "Between" is also acceptable for more than two when each item is considered individually (e.g., treaties between the four states).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

At the core of the (1) ______ lies the fierce (2) ______ between two branches of the Kuru dynasty, the Pandavas and the Kauravas. The lifelong struggle (3) ______ the cousins for the throne of Hastinapur culminates (4) ______ bloody battle of Kurukshetra, in which (5) ______ kings of that period participated and perished.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. in the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "culminate" takes the preposition "in" — to culminate in something means to reach its final and highest point in that thing. The following noun phrase "bloody battle of Kurukshetra" is a specific, uniquely identified battle, so it needs the definite article "the". Hence "in the bloody battle of Kurukshetra". (परिणत होना)

◦ Correct: ... culminates in the bloody battle of Kurukshetra ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "in that" would need a clause after it, not a noun phrase.

• Option 2 "inside" wrongly suggests physical location and drops the required article.

• Option 4 "in to" is a wrong split; "into" (one word) shows movement, and "culminate into" is not standard English.

NOTE

• Verb + preposition combinations frequently tested: culminate in, result in, consist of, comprise (no preposition), insist on, object to, depend on, deprive of. Use "the" before unique or already-specified nouns (the battle of Kurukshetra, the Ganga, the Sun).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

At the core of the (1) ______ lies the fierce (2) ______ between two branches of the Kuru dynasty, the Pandavas and the Kauravas. The lifelong struggle (3) ______ the cousins for the throne of Hastinapur culminates (4) ______ bloody battle of Kurukshetra, in which (5) ______ kings of that period participated and perished.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. most.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed directly by the plural countable noun "kings", so it needs a quantifier meaning "the greater part of". "Most kings of that period participated and perished" is the correct and idiomatic reading. (अधिकांश)

◦ Correct: ... the bloody battle of Kurukshetra, in which most kings of that period participated and perished.

• "Most + plural noun + plural verb (participated)" agrees perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "total" is an adjective/noun used with amounts ("the total number of kings"), not directly as a quantifier before a plural noun in this sense.

• Option 2 "almost" is an adverb and cannot modify a noun on its own; it would have to be "almost all kings".

• Option 4 "each" takes a singular noun and a singular verb ("each king participates"), which clashes with "kings ... participated".

NOTE

• Quantifier rules: most/many/few/several + plural noun; much/little + uncountable noun; each/every + singular countable noun. "Almost" must be paired with all/every/no ("almost all", "almost every", "almost no").

question: The statement- "We shall die to awaken the nation" was made by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bagha Jatin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous statement "We shall die to awaken the nation" was made by the Bengali revolutionary Jatindranath Mukherjee, popularly known as "Bagha Jatin". (बाघा जतिन)

• He earned the title "Bagha" ("tiger") after killing a Royal Bengal tiger with a dagger.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bagha Jatin was a principal leader of the Jugantar revolutionary party in Bengal and was linked with the Indo-German Conspiracy during the First World War.

• He was fatally wounded in the Battle of Balasore (September 1915) against the British police in Odisha and died the next day.

NOTE

• Option 2 Pingali Venkayya designed the flag on which the Indian national flag is based.

• Option 3 Bir Tikendrajit Singh was the Manipuri prince who led resistance in the Anglo-Manipur War (1891).

• Option 4 Surya Sen (Masterda) led the Chittagong Armoury Raid (1930).

question: Liver gland secretes ______ that is stored in a sac called the gall bladder.
solution_text:
The correct answer is bile juice.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The liver, the largest gland in the human body, secretes "bile juice", which is stored and concentrated in a small sac called the gall bladder and released into the duodenum through the bile duct. (पित्त रस — पित्ताशय में संग्रहित)

• Bile contains bile salts that emulsify fats — they break large fat globules into small droplets so that the enzyme lipase can digest them. Bile is alkaline and also makes the acidic food from the stomach suitable for intestinal enzymes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Estrogen is a female sex hormone secreted mainly by the ovaries.

• Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is secreted by the oxyntic (parietal) cells of the stomach; it kills germs and activates pepsinogen into pepsin.

• Mucus is secreted by goblet cells and protects the stomach lining from acid.

NOTE

• The liver also stores glycogen, produces urea, detoxifies harmful substances and stores vitamins A, D, E, K and B12. Bile itself contains no digestive enzyme.

question: Which of the following government official is the ex officio chairman of Rajya Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vice President of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 64 of the Constitution, the Vice President of India is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (the Council of States) and holds no other office of profit. Article 89(1) also states that the Vice President shall be ex officio Chairman of the Council of States. (उपराष्ट्रपति — राज्यसभा के पदेन सभापति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is elected by the members of the Rajya Sabha from amongst themselves (Article 89(2)).

• The Lok Sabha is presided over by the Speaker, who is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha.

• The Vice President is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament (elected + nominated) by proportional representation with a single transferable vote.

NOTE

• The Vice President acts as President when the office falls vacant (Article 65). Minimum age to become Vice President: 35 years; term: 5 years.

question: In 2019, the Government of India honoured Milena Salvini, an Italian-born Kathakali dancer, with which of the following award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Shri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2019, the Government of India conferred the "Padma Shri" on Milena Salvini, the Italian-born (French-based) Kathakali exponent and scholar, for her lifelong work in popularising Indian classical dance in Europe. (पद्म श्री — मिलेना साल्विनी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Padma Awards are announced every year on the eve of Republic Day and are given in three grades:

◦ Padma Vibhushan — for exceptional and distinguished service (second-highest civilian award).

◦ Padma Bhushan — for distinguished service of a high order (third-highest).

◦ Padma Shri — for distinguished service in any field (fourth-highest).

• The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award, instituted in 1954.

NOTE

• Kathakali is the classical dance-drama of Kerala, famous for its elaborate green/red make-up (chutti), huge costumes and stories drawn from the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

question: How many laws were repealed under the Farm Laws Repeal Bill, 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Three.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Farm Laws Repeal Bill, 2021 repealed the three farm laws enacted in September 2020. (तीन कृषि कानून निरस्त)

◦ The Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2020

◦ The Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, 2020

◦ The Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The repeal was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 19 November 2021 (Guru Nanak Jayanti) after a year-long farmers' agitation.

• The Bill was passed by both Houses of Parliament on 29 November 2021 in the Winter Session and received the President's assent on 1 December 2021.

NOTE

• Agriculture is a State subject (Entry 14, State List), while trade and commerce in foodstuffs falls under the Concurrent List (Entry 33) — the constitutional point around which much of the farm-laws debate revolved.

question: Provida style of architecture belongs to which empire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vijayanagar Empire.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Provida (Pravida) style" of temple architecture is associated with the Vijayanagara Empire (1336–1646) of South India. It is essentially a rich elaboration of the Dravida style, marked by towering gopurams, huge pillared mandapas, kalyana mandapas and richly carved monolithic pillars. (विजयनगर साम्राज्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I of the Sangama dynasty, with its capital at Hampi on the Tungabhadra river.

• Its greatest ruler was Krishnadeva Raya (1509–1529) of the Tuluva dynasty, in whose reign the Vitthala Temple and Hazara Rama Temple were built.

• Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site; the empire declined after the Battle of Talikota (1565).

NOTE

• The three classical temple styles: Nagara (North India, curvilinear shikhara), Dravida (South India, pyramidal vimana with gopurams) and Vesara (a hybrid style of the Deccan, developed by the Chalukyas and Hoysalas).

question: In January 2022, former RBI Governor, Urjit Patel has been appointed as vice-president for investment operations in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In January 2022, Dr Urjit Patel, the former (24th) Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, was appointed a Vice-President for investment operations at the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB). (एशियन इन्फ्रास्ट्रक्चर इन्वेस्टमेंट बैंक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The AIIB is a multilateral development bank headquartered in Beijing, China, which began operations in January 2016. India is its second-largest shareholder after China and its largest borrower.

• Urjit Patel served as RBI Governor from September 2016 to December 2018 (the demonetisation period) and earlier headed the committee that recommended inflation targeting and the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) framework.

NOTE

• Other multilateral institutions: World Bank (HQ Washington DC), IMF (HQ Washington DC), New Development Bank/BRICS Bank (HQ Shanghai, first President K. V. Kamath), ADB (HQ Manila).

question: The Great Rann of Kutch falls into ______ region of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thar Desert.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Great Rann of Kutch, a vast salt marsh in the Kutch district of Gujarat, lies in the Thar Desert region of India. It is one of the largest salt deserts in the world. (थार मरुस्थल — कच्छ का रण)

• During the monsoon the Rann is flooded with sea water and river water; in the dry season it turns into a dazzling white expanse of salt.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Rann Utsav, a famous cultural festival, is held here every winter.

• The Indian Wild Ass (Ghudkhur) Sanctuary is located in the Little Rann of Kutch; the Great Rann is famous for the breeding colonies of the Greater Flamingo (Flamingo City).

• The Thar Desert (Great Indian Desert) spreads over Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab and Haryana and extends into Pakistan.

NOTE

• India's physiographic divisions: the Northern Mountains, the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands.

question: Which among the following states does NOT produce coal in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given options, Gujarat is not a producer of coal (it produces lignite, the inferior brown coal, at Panandhro and Kutch, but not true coal). India's coal is overwhelmingly produced by Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh. (गुजरात — कोयला उत्पादक नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Major coalfields: Jharia, Bokaro, Giridih and Karanpura (Jharkhand); Talcher and Ib Valley (Odisha); Korba (Chhattisgarh); Singrauli (Madhya Pradesh); Raniganj (West Bengal); Singareni (Telangana).

• Most Indian coal belongs to the Gondwana formations (about 98%); the rest is Tertiary coal found in the North-East, Jammu and Kashmir.

NOTE

• Types of coal by carbon content (highest to lowest): Anthracite > Bituminous > Lignite > Peat. Coal India Limited (CIL), a Maharatna PSU headquartered in Kolkata, is the world's largest coal-producing company.

question: Mohenjodaro belongs to which of the following civilization?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indus Valley civilization.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mohenjodaro ("Mound of the Dead"), on the right bank of the Indus in the Larkana district of Sindh, Pakistan, is one of the largest cities of the Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilization. It was discovered in 1922 by R. D. Banerji. (सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता — मोहनजोदड़ो)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Famous finds at Mohenjodaro: the Great Bath, the Great Granary, the bronze Dancing Girl, the steatite Bearded Priest-King, and the Pashupati seal.

• The Indus Valley Civilization (c. 2500–1750 BCE) was a Bronze Age urban civilization noted for grid-pattern town planning, burnt-brick houses, covered drainage and standardised weights.

• Other major sites: Harappa (Ravi), Kalibangan (Ghaggar), Lothal and Dholavira (Gujarat), Rakhigarhi (Haryana — largest site in India), Banawali and Chanhudaro.

NOTE

• Mohenjodaro is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Harappa was the first site excavated (by Daya Ram Sahni in 1921), which is why the civilization is also called the Harappan Civilization.

question: By which process, water soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Leaching.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Leaching" is the process in which water-soluble inorganic nutrients percolate down (with water) into the lower soil horizons and get precipitated there as unavailable salts, making them inaccessible to plant roots. (निक्षालन)

• Leaching is one of the steps in the decomposition process of the ecosystem, along with fragmentation, catabolism, humification and mineralisation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Fragmentation — detritivores (e.g., earthworms) break down detritus into smaller particles.

• Catabolism — bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances.

• Humification — accumulation of a dark-coloured amorphous substance called humus, which is highly resistant to microbial action and acts as a reservoir of nutrients.

• Mineralisation — humus is further degraded by microbes to release inorganic nutrients.

NOTE

• Decomposition is largely an oxygen-requiring (aerobic) process; its rate is controlled by the chemical composition of detritus and by climatic factors such as temperature and soil moisture.

question: Super Bowl, an annual championship game of Football is held in _______ country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is United States of America.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Super Bowl" is the annual championship game of the National Football League (NFL) and is held in the United States of America. It decides the champion of American football and is one of the most watched sporting events in the world. (संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका)

• The first Super Bowl was played in 1967; the winning team receives the Vince Lombardi Trophy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Super Bowl half-time show is a globally famous musical performance, and Super Bowl Sunday is informally one of the biggest days of the American sporting calendar.

• "Football" in the USA means American football (played with an oval ball), which is different from association football (soccer).

NOTE

• Championship/trophy links: NFL – Super Bowl; NBA – NBA Finals (basketball); MLB – World Series (baseball); NHL – Stanley Cup (ice hockey).

question: Which among the following festivals mark the start of Telugu New year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ugadi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ugadi" (also spelt Yugadi) marks the beginning of the New Year for the people of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka — that is, the Telugu (and Kannada) New Year. It falls on the first day of the Hindu month of Chaitra (March–April). (उगादी — तेलुगु नववर्ष)

• The word comes from Sanskrit "Yuga" (age) + "Adi" (beginning). A special dish called Ugadi Pachadi, mixing six tastes, symbolises the different experiences of life.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Gudi Padwa is the New Year festival of Maharashtra (same day as Ugadi).

• Onam is the harvest festival of Kerala, associated with King Mahabali.

• Pongal is the four-day harvest festival of Tamil Nadu, celebrated in mid-January (Makar Sankranti time).

NOTE

• Other regional New Years: Baisakhi (Punjab), Bihu (Assam), Puthandu (Tamil Nadu), Vishu (Kerala), Poila Boishakh (West Bengal), Navreh (Kashmir), Cheti Chand (Sindhi).

question: Which among the following planets rotates in a direction opposite to that of the others?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Venus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Venus rotates on its axis from east to west (clockwise, when seen from above the north pole) — the direction opposite to that of almost all the other planets, which rotate west to east (anticlockwise). This is called retrograde rotation. (शुक्र — विपरीत दिशा में घूर्णन)

• On Venus, therefore, the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Uranus also has an unusual rotation — it is tilted by about 98° and effectively rolls on its side.

• Venus is the hottest planet (about 462 °C) because of a runaway greenhouse effect caused by its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere.

• Venus is called the "Morning Star"/"Evening Star" and the twin/sister of the Earth because of its similar size and mass. It is the brightest planet in our sky.

NOTE

• Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate once but only about 225 Earth days to revolve around the Sun — so its day is longer than its year.

question: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is best known for which of the following instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarod.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is one of India's greatest Sarod maestros, belonging to the Senia Bangash gharana of Gwalior. (सरोद — उस्ताद अमजद अली खान)

• The sarod is a fretless, plucked string instrument with a metal fingerboard and a deep, resonant tone, widely used in Hindustani classical music.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Amjad Ali Khan has been honoured with the Padma Vibhushan, the Padma Bhushan, the Padma Shri and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. His sons Amaan Ali Bangash and Ayaan Ali Bangash are also sarod players.

• Other sarod exponents: Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan (his father).

NOTE

• Instrument–artist pairs: Santoor – Pandit Shivkumar Sharma; Shehnai – Ustad Bismillah Khan; Sitar – Pandit Ravi Shankar; Flute – Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia; Tabla – Ustad Zakir Hussain; Violin – Dr L. Subramaniam; Mandolin – U. Srinivas.

question: The UMEED Scheme of ______ Rural Livelihoods Mission is providing help to the aspirations of rural women in the Union Territory, who aspire to become economically independent.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jammu and Kashmir.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "UMEED" is the Jammu and Kashmir State Rural Livelihoods Mission (JKRLM), which mobilises rural women into Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and helps them become economically independent through skill training, credit linkage and livelihood support. (उम्मीद योजना — जम्मू-कश्मीर)

• The question itself indicates a Union Territory, and Jammu and Kashmir has been a UT since 31 October 2019.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• UMEED works under the umbrella of the national Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) of the Ministry of Rural Development.

• The mission promotes SHGs, Village Organisations and Cluster Level Federations, providing revolving funds and bank linkage for micro-enterprises.

NOTE

• India currently has 8 Union Territories: Delhi, Puducherry, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Chandigarh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

question: Who wrote book named "Gulamgiri" in 1873?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jyotiba Phule.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gulamgiri" ("Slavery"), published in 1873, was written by the great social reformer Jyotirao (Jyotiba) Phule of Maharashtra. In it he attacked the caste system and compared the condition of the lower castes in India with that of the black slaves in America. (गुलामगिरी — ज्योतिबा फुले)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Society of Truth Seekers) in 1873 at Pune to secure rights for the depressed classes.

• With his wife Savitribai Phule, he opened the first school for girls in India (Pune, 1848) and worked for widow remarriage and against untouchability. He was given the title "Mahatma" in 1888.

• His other works include Shetkaryacha Asud (Cultivator's Whipcord) and Tritiya Ratna.

NOTE

• Debendranath Tagore founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha and led the Brahmo Samaj; Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj (1875) and wrote Satyarth Prakash; Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar championed widow remarriage (Act of 1856).

question: The World Games 2022 was held in ______ city of the country, United States of America.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Birmingham.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 11th World Games (2022) were held in Birmingham, Alabama, United States of America, from 7 to 17 July 2022. (बर्मिंघम, अलबामा)

• The event was originally scheduled for 2021 but was postponed by a year because the Tokyo Olympics were shifted to 2021 due to COVID-19.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The World Games is a multi-sport event held every four years for sports that are not part of the Olympic Games — such as tug of war, korfball, sumo, powerlifting, lacrosse, air sports and roller sports. It is governed by the International World Games Association (IWGA), founded in 1980, in cooperation with the IOC.

• The first World Games were held in Santa Clara, USA, in 1981. The 2025 edition was held in Chengdu, China.

NOTE

• Do not confuse the World Games with the Olympic Games, the Commonwealth Games (every 4 years, Commonwealth nations) or the Asian Games (every 4 years, Asia).

question: The famous movie "3 idiots" is based on the novel "Five Point Someone" which is written by Indian author ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chetan Bhagat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bollywood film "3 Idiots" (2009), directed by Rajkumar Hirani, is based on the novel "Five Point Someone – What not to do at IIT!" (2004) written by Chetan Bhagat. (चेतन भगत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other novels by Chetan Bhagat and their film adaptations: One Night @ the Call Center → Hello; The 3 Mistakes of My Life → Kai Po Che!; 2 States → 2 States; Half Girlfriend → Half Girlfriend.

• Chetan Bhagat is an alumnus of IIT Delhi and IIM Ahmedabad.

NOTE

• Khushwant Singh wrote Train to Pakistan and The Company of Women; Durjoy Datta wrote Of Course I Love You; Novoneel Chakraborty wrote the Stranger trilogy.

question: The minimum rate below which banks are not allowed to lend money except in cases specified by the Reserve Bank of India is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is base rate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "base rate" is the minimum lending rate fixed by a bank below which it is not permitted to lend to any customer, except in cases specified by the Reserve Bank of India. It was introduced by the RBI on 1 July 2010, replacing the earlier Benchmark Prime Lending Rate (BPLR) system, to bring transparency to loan pricing. (आधार दर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Repo rate — the rate at which the RBI lends short-term money to commercial banks against government securities.

• Reverse repo rate — the rate at which the RBI borrows money from commercial banks (absorbs liquidity).

• From April 2016 the RBI introduced the MCLR (Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate) and from October 2019 the External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR) for new retail loans.

NOTE

• Other RBI monetary tools: CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio), SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio), Bank Rate, MSF (Marginal Standing Facility) and Open Market Operations (OMOs). Rates are decided by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), a six-member body headed by the RBI Governor.

question: As of November 2022, what is the official language of India's neighbouring country China?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mandarin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The official language of the People's Republic of China is Standard Chinese, popularly known as "Mandarin" (Putonghua). It is written in Chinese characters and is the most widely spoken first language in the world. (मंदारिन — चीन की राजभाषा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• China — capital Beijing, currency Renminbi/Yuan; it shares the Line of Actual Control (LAC) with India.

• Sinhala (with Tamil) is the official language of Sri Lanka; Burmese is the official language of Myanmar; Bengali is the official language of Bangladesh.

NOTE

• India's neighbours and their capitals/currencies: Pakistan (Islamabad, Rupee), Nepal (Kathmandu, Nepalese Rupee), Bhutan (Thimphu, Ngultrum), Bangladesh (Dhaka, Taka), Myanmar (Nay Pyi Taw, Kyat), Sri Lanka (Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, Sri Lankan Rupee), Afghanistan (Kabul, Afghani), Maldives (Male, Rufiyaa).

question: Ananga Pala was a ruler of which dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajput Dynasty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Anangpal (Ananga Pala) Tomar was a ruler of the Tomar (Tomara) Rajput dynasty, which ruled the Delhi region in the 11th–12th centuries. He is traditionally credited with founding Dhillika (Delhi) and building the Lal Kot, the first of the seven cities of Delhi, around 1052 CE. (तोमर राजपूत वंश — अनंगपाल)

• The famous Iron Pillar was, according to tradition, brought to the Delhi complex during his reign.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Tomars were later displaced by the Chauhans (Chahamanas); Prithviraj Chauhan III was defeated by Muhammad Ghori in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), which paved the way for the Delhi Sultanate.

• The Gurjara-Pratiharas ruled from Kannauj (Mihir Bhoja was the greatest ruler); the Pallavas ruled from Kanchipuram (Mahendravarman I, Narasimhavarman I); the Khalji dynasty (1290–1320) was a Delhi Sultanate dynasty (Alauddin Khalji).

NOTE

• The "seven cities of Delhi": Lal Kot/Qila Rai Pithora, Siri, Tughlaqabad, Jahanpanah, Firozabad, Din Panah (Purana Qila) and Shahjahanabad.

question: Formula to find unemployment rate is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is (Unemployed workers/Total labour force) × 100.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The unemployment rate is the percentage of the labour force that is unemployed but actively seeking work:

◦ Unemployment Rate = (Number of unemployed persons ÷ Total labour force) × 100

• The labour force = employed persons + unemployed persons who are willing and able to work and are actively looking for work. (बेरोज़गारी दर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly restricts the numerator to male workers and multiplies by 1000.

• Options 3 and 4 use "employed workers", which would give the employment rate, not the unemployment rate.

• In India, employment/unemployment data are collected through the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by the NSO (National Statistical Office) since 2017-18; the private CMIE also publishes monthly estimates.

NOTE

• Types of unemployment: disguised (more workers than needed, common in agriculture), seasonal, structural, cyclical, frictional and educated unemployment. Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) = (labour force ÷ population) × 100.

question: Which among the following dance forms of India is associated with Rajasthan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghoomar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ghoomar" is a traditional folk dance of Rajasthan, performed by women in flowing ghagras who move in a graceful circular motion — the name comes from "ghoomna" (to whirl). It is associated especially with the Bhil community and the Rajput royal households, and is performed on festivals such as Teej, Gangaur and Holi. (घूमर — राजस्थान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu; Odissi is the classical dance of Odisha; Charkula is a folk dance of the Braj region of Uttar Pradesh in which a woman balances a large multi-tiered lamp-pyramid on her head.

• Other folk dances of Rajasthan: Kalbeliya (a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage), Kathputli, Chari, Bhavai, Terah Taali and Gair.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: The force exerted by a charged body on another charged or uncharged body is known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is electrostatic force.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The force exerted by a charged body on another charged or uncharged body is called the "electrostatic force" (or electric force). It is a non-contact force — it acts even without the bodies touching. (स्थिर वैद्युत बल)

• Like charges repel and unlike charges attract. A charged body can also attract an uncharged (neutral) body by induction, e.g., a comb rubbed on dry hair picks up small bits of paper.

• Coulomb's law: F = k·q₁q₂/r² — the force is directly proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Gravitational force — the attractive force between any two masses (always attractive, and the weakest of the four fundamental forces).

• Frictional force — a contact force that opposes relative motion between surfaces.

• "Pressure force" is not a standard named force; pressure = force per unit area (P = F/A).

NOTE

• The four fundamental forces in nature, from strongest to weakest: Strong nuclear > Electromagnetic > Weak nuclear > Gravitational. The SI unit of charge is the coulomb (C) and of force the newton (N).
